2 Shariatpur 'Razakars' again linked to killings
2016-07-26T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/2-shariatpur-razakars-again-linked-killings-1259566

A prosecution witness yesterday gave a testimony linking, as had most of the six others before him, two alleged Shariatpur Razakars to killings of scores of people and rape of women during the 1971 Liberation War.

Facing four charges, Sulaiman Mollah is now in jail and pleads not guilty while Edris Ali Sarder is on the run.

Anil Chandra Das, 61, told International Crimes Tribunal-1 that Sulaiman, Edris and other Razakars and the Pakistani occupation army men killed around 200 people attacking Kashabhog and Madyapara villages under Palang Police Station on May 22.

He came to know about it from fleeing villagers taking shelter in his home village of Dhanuka, he said.

The next day, Razakars including Sulaiman and Edris and the Pakistani army men attacked Malopara village and took 30 to 35 people including women to a Pakistani army camp set up at AR Hawlader Jute Mill in Madaripur, he said.

He said to have gone to the village a few days later and heard from some of the victims and their relatives that the women were released after being raped for three days and the men killed. In mid-June, Sulaiman and Edris along with eight to 10 Razakars and 10 to 15 Pakistani army men came to the house of his neighbour, Mukunda Lal Paul, said Anil.

He said to have watched hiding in a bush with some others as the Pakistani army men bayoneted two guards, Sukrai Goon and Lalit Mohan Kundu, and threw them off the house's first floor.

They found the two dead after the attackers left, he said.

A defence counsel cross examined Anil before the three-member tribunal led by Justice Anwarul Haque adjourned proceedings until today.
